frase_gancho.texto: From the desert to the sierra: peoples who dance, weave, and carve their freedom.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: You leave the south behind and arrive in the vast landscapes of the northwest: desert, sierra, and coast. Here live the Yaqui, the Mayo, the Rarámuri or Tarahumara, the Seri, and other peoples, who learned to adapt to dry lands and great distances. The Yaqui and the Rarámuri speak languages of the same great family as Nahuatl; the Seri, by contrast, speak a language with no known relatives. This hall brings together a Holy Week mask, a violin from the sierra, a woven plate, and a sculpture made of very hard wood. They are objects from peoples who have cared for their land and their festivals for centuries.
